Subject: escalation - recurring CRM data-quality complaints from the field

I'm writing this up on behalf of Customer Success. Over the past few sprints our
account managers have logged a run of small but genuine mistakes in how the contact
tooling saves and shows two fields: a contact's mobile number and their loan type.
Every one of these has been reproduced on a live account, so please treat them as
real defects rather than user error. They only bite when a contact's details come in
a slightly off-pattern shape, which is why they slipped past everyone for weeks - the
routine cases (a plain US mobile, a loan type chosen from the dropdown) come out
perfectly correct, and our automated checks only ever exercise those routine cases.

Here is what the managers actually reported, in their words:

- "I onboarded a borrower in London and typed their mobile the way it's printed on
  their letterhead. Our workspace is configured to default to the UK, but the number
  saved under a US code (+1...) instead of the UK code (+44...)." So: when the digits
  could belong to more than one country, the contact's configured home region is being
  ignored and the wrong country is winning.

- "A few contacts gave me their number in the international style that starts with a
  double-zero access code - a 0044 UK number, for instance. Instead of accepting it,
  the tool told me the number was invalid and I had to retype it by hand." So: the 00
  international prefix isn't being treated as equivalent to a leading +.

- "One of my older accounts is tagged with a loan type from before we cleaned up the
  catalog, and the label on the record printed as 'Hardmoney' - no space - when it
  should read 'Hard Money', same word-by-word capitalization as every other loan type
  we display." So: an unfamiliar loan-type code isn't being turned into a readable,
  properly spaced and capitalized label.

- "A rep entered a loan type as 'Working_Capital', with the odd capitals and the
  underscore, and that's exactly the string that got stored on the contact - not the
  tidy internal code the rest of the system matches against." So: an oddly-cased entry
  of a known type is being stored verbatim rather than normalized to its standard code.

There may be more corners like these; those are simply the ones we could reproduce.
The common thread is that all of it is pure string-and-lookup work - deciding a
country for a number, reshaping a dialed number into storage form, and mapping a
loan-type string to its code and its display label. No database or network calls are
involved, so each case is reproducible from a direct call.

What I need from engineering: make the saved and displayed values correct for these
unusual-but-legitimate inputs, and do it without disturbing how the ordinary inputs
(the ones our current checks cover) already behave. Please don't touch the existing
test files, and confirm the current suite still passes when you're done:

    cd /app/loangen-agent && python -m pytest tests -v

Research complete. Here is the full report.

# 1. Overall directory structure

```
/app/loangen-agent/
├── agent/                      # Main application package (~290 .py files)
│   ├── core/                   # config.py (Settings), email/, logging
│   ├── integrations/
│   │   ├── cartesia/           # phone.py  <-- core phone normalization
│   │   ├── twilio/             # __init__.py has mask_phone()
│   │   ├── lendflow/, quickbooks/
│   ├── services/
│   │   ├── smbcontacts/        # loan_types.py <-- canonical loan-type registry; service.py (CSV import, contact CRUD, call initiation)
│   │   ├── smbinvites/         # invite conversation flow (uses loan types)
│   │   ├── smbapplications/, calls/ (service.py, inbound.py), contactleads/,
│   │   │   cre_qualification/ (engine, lender_match.py, qualification_report_pdf.py, required_docs.py),
│   │   │   loanproducts/, prequal/, waitlist/, notifications/, documentrequests/, feedback/
│   │   ├── analytics/, auth/, billing/, chat/, credit/, documents/, llm/, plaid/,
│   │   │   prompts/, seed/, storage/, tools/, voice_agent/, observability/, array/
├── tests/                      # 33 flat test files (unittest-style)
├── training/                   # fine-tuning / synthetic data scripts
├── docs/, deploy/, docker/
├── .env.example, requirements.txt, README.md, Dockerfile, docker-compose.yml
```

# 2. Phone number parsing / normalization

### Core module: `/app/loangen-agent/agent/integrations/cartesia/phone.py` (154 lines)

Uses the `phonenumbers` library. Two entry points:

**`try_normalize_phone_to_e164(raw, *, default_region=None)` — lines 44–105** (best-effort, for CRM storage; returns `Optional[str]`)
- Strips whitespace; **"00" prefix handling (line 60–61):** `value = "+" + value[2:]` — replaces both zeros with `+` (correct conversion, e.g. `0091...` → `+91...`).
- Cleans non-digit chars via `_NON_DIGIT_RE = re.compile(r"[^\d+]+")` (line 16).
- If it starts with `+`: parse with region `None`, first requiring `is_valid_number`, then falling back to `is_possible_number` (lines 67–72).
- **Country/region selection when no `+` (lines 74–97):** builds a region list — default region first, then a hardcoded fallback list `_CRM_FALLBACK_REGIONS = ("US", "CA", "IN", "GB", "AU", "MX", "DE", "FR")` (line 19). Tries each region; collects *valid* matches and *possible* matches separately. Returns first valid match; otherwise the **last** possible match. Note a subtle bug at lines 76–78: `if not default: regions.append(default)` — the configured default region is only appended when it's *empty*, so a non-US default region is effectively never inserted ahead of the fallback tuple (US always goes first).
- Last-resort digit heuristics (lines 99–104): 10 digits → `+1{digits}`; 11 digits starting with 1 → `+{digits}`; 8–15 digits → `+{digits}`; else `None`.

**`normalize_phone_to_e164(raw, *, default_region=None)` — lines 108–154** (strict; raises `ValueError`)
- **"00" prefix handling (lines 123–125):** `value = "+" + value[1:]` — only strips *one* character, producing `+0...` (inconsistent with the `value[2:]` logic in the try_ variant; looks like a bug).
- If cleaned value starts with `+`: parse with `region=None`; else parse with `region = (default_region or "US").strip().upper()` (`_FALLBACK_REGION = "US"`, line 17).
- Requires both `is_possible_number` and `is_valid_number`; error messages suggest setting `CARTESIA_DEFAULT_PHONE_REGION`. Formats to `PhoneNumberFormat.E164`.

### Configuration
- `agent/core/config.py` line 248: `cartesia_default_phone_region: str = "US"`; validator at lines 319–324 coerces None/blank to `"US"`. `.env.example` line 470: `CARTESIA_DEFAULT_PHONE_REGION=US`.

### Call sites
- `agent/services/smbcontacts/service.py`:
  - `_default_phone_region()` line 89–90 (settings value or "US")
  - `normalize_mobile_for_storage()` line 93 (strict), `try_normalize_mobile()` line 98 (lenient)
  - `_mobile_from_input_or_error()` line 102 (create/update; 400 `INVALID_MOBILE_NUMBER` on failure)
  - `_resolve_mobile_for_import()` line 122 (CSV import; stores `""` + warning on failure)
  - `_normalize_contact_phone()` line 569 (before AI/direct calls; 400 on missing/invalid)
- `agent/services/calls/service.py` `build_inbound_twiml()` lines 1776–1790: normalizes inbound Twilio caller ID with strict function + default region.
- `agent/services/calls/inbound.py` `_find_contact_for_lender_phone()` lines 182–204: matches caller by last-10-digit regex on `SMBContact.mobile`, then confirms by re-normalizing each candidate; `resolve_inbound_route()` line 108.
- `agent/integrations/twilio/__init__.py` `mask_phone()` lines 375–379: masks to `***-***-1234`.
- `agent/services/contactleads/schemas.py` `validate_phone()` lines 46–56: simple regex format check only (`_PHONE_RE`, 7–20 chars), no E.164 normalization.

# 3. Loan type normalization / display

There are **two separate systems** (note: no "hard_money" exists anywhere in the codebase — greps for `hard_money`/`Hard Money` return nothing; it would only hit the generic fallback paths below).

### A. CRM canonical registry: `/app/loangen-agent/agent/services/smbcontacts/loan_types.py` (119 lines)
- `LOAN_TYPE_CHOICES` lines 12–33: 20 canonical `{id, label}` entries (`sba7a`, `sba504`, `term`, `loc`, `cre`, `bridge`, `mca`, `rbf`, `abl`, `usda`, …).
- `_EXTRA_ALIASES` lines 38–81: alias strings → canonical id (e.g. `"line of credit"` → `"loc"`).
- `_normalize_key()` lines 84–85: lowercases, converts `_`/`-` to spaces.
- `resolve_loan_type(raw)` lines 97–115: try compact form (strip spaces/dashes/underscores) against ids → lowercased raw against ids → alias map → label/id match after key normalization → `None`.
- `loan_type_label(loan_type_id)` lines 88–94: looks up label by id; **fallback is `loan_type_id.replace("_", "").title()`** — note it removes underscores *without* inserting a space, so a hypothetical `hard_money` would become `"Hardmoney"`, not `"Hard Money"` (inconsistent with the other formatters below).
- `is_valid_loan_type_id()` lines 118–119.
- Consumers: `smbcontacts/schemas.py` validators (lines 82–90, 146), `smbcontacts/service.py` `_parse_loan_type_from_csv()` lines 161–185 (CSV import with warning on unrecognized type), `smbinvites/schemas.py` `validate_loan_type_id` (lines 16–24), `smbinvites/service.py` (CRM-hint confirm step at lines 442–466 using `loan_type_label`; strict id validation at lines 1230–1235).

### B. Qualification display/matching: `/app/loangen-agent/agent/services/cre_qualification/lender_match.py`
- `_LOAN_TYPE_LABELS` lines 20–31: separate, smaller mapping (`"term"` → `"Term Loan"`, `"cre"` → `"Commercial Real Estate"`, `"rehab"` → `"Rehab / Value-Add"`, …).
- `format_application_loan_type(loan_type)` lines 46–56: empty → `"—"`; compacts key (lowercase, strip `_`/`-`) and matches against label keys, also substring match `k in raw.lower()`; **fallback `raw.replace("_", " ").title()`** — this is the path that turns `"hard_money"` into `"Hard Money"`.
- `product_matches_application_loan_type(product, loan_type, loan_purpose, *, has_cre_deal)` lines 67–118: keyword matching of catalog product name/category (SBA, LOC, equipment, term, real-estate, revenue-based) against loan type/purpose text; returns `(matches, reason)` for UI badges; CRE purpose-based match excluded when borrower explicitly chose term/SBA/LOC/equipment (lines 104–113).
- Used in `cre_qualification/engine.py` (lines 1377, 1414, 1463) for display and match badges.

### C. PDF report formatter: `/app/loangen-agent/agent/services/cre_qualification/qualification_report_pdf.py`
- `_format_loan_type(raw)` lines 221–224: simple `raw.replace("_", " ").strip().title()` (also would give `"Hard Money"`), used at lines 353–376.

Also related: `cre_qualification/required_docs.py` — `_REQUIRED_BY_LOAN_TYPE` (line 8), `required_document_types()` line 133, `infer_deal_profile()` line ~148 (keyword-based loan-type bucketing for doc requirements).

# 4. Tests

All tests live flat in `/app/loangen-agent/tests/` (33 files, unittest style).

**Phone coverage:**
- `tests/test_smb_contacts_csv_and_update.py` — `PhoneNormalizationTests` (lines 30–61): US formatting `(512) 555-0142` → `+1…`; **Indian 10-digit number without country code under US default region → `+918050306043`** (exercises the multi-region fallback); explicit `+91…` passthrough; garbage → `None`. Also CSV import phone behavior (lines 64–145: missing mobile imports with warning, duplicate-email update sets `+13027373362`) and PATCH international update (lines 231–257).
- `tests/test_inbound_calls.py` — mocks `normalize_phone_to_e164` (lines 180, 222, 266) to test inbound routing/TwiML, plus `_find_last_outbound_to_phone` / `_find_contact_for_lender_phone` routing logic; not the parser itself.
- **No dedicated test file for `agent/integrations/cartesia/phone.py` directly** — notably, there are **no tests for the "00" prefix path** in either function (where the two implementations disagree), and no test that a non-US `cartesia_default_phone_region` is honored.

**Loan type coverage:**
- `tests/test_smb_contacts_csv_and_update.py` — `LoanTypeResolverTests` (lines 16–27): canonical id, label (`"SBA 7(a) Loan"` → `sba7a`), alias (`"line of credit"` → `loc`), unknown → `None`. CSV import warning for `bad-type` (lines 65–87).
- `tests/test_smb_invite_schemas.py` — `loan_type_id` validation (accept `sba7a`, reject unknown, None allowed).
- `tests/test_smb_invite_conversation.py` — CRM `loan_type` hint flows into invite state (`crm_hint_loan_type`).
- `tests/test_lender_product_match.py` — `format_application_loan_type("term")` → `"Term Loan"` (line 20) and product-match logic (term vs SBA vs CRE, `has_cre_deal` behavior).
- `tests/test_required_docs.py`, `tests/test_cre_qualification.py`, `tests/test_qualification_report_pdf.py`, `tests/test_bridge_broadway_qualification.py` — use loan-type strings (`"Construction"`, `"Commercial Real Estate"`, `"term"`) to drive doc requirements / qualification, incidental coverage only. **No tests exist for `loan_type_label` fallback or `_format_loan_type` in the PDF module.**

# Notable observations (current-behavior quirks)

1. **"00" prefix inconsistency** in `phone.py`: `try_normalize_phone_to_e164` line 61 uses `value[2:]` (correct), while `normalize_phone_to_e164` line 125 uses `value[1:]`, leaving a stray `0` after the `+` (likely bug; untested).
2. **Default region ordering bug** in `try_normalize_phone_to_e164` lines 76–78: the configured default region is only appended to the candidate list when it's falsy, so a configured non-US region never actually takes priority — US (first fallback region) always wins.
3. **Label-format inconsistency**: `loan_type_label` fallback (`replace("_", "")` → `"Hardmoney"`) vs `format_application_loan_type` / `_format_loan_type` fallbacks (`replace("_", " ")` → `"Hard Money"`); and two independent id→label maps (`LOAN_TYPE_CHOICES` vs `_LOAN_TYPE_LABELS`) with differing labels for `cre` ("Commercial Real Estate Loan" vs "Commercial Real Estate").

1: """
2: E.164 phone normalization for Cartesia outbound calls.
3: 
4: Numbers may be stored with or without a + country code. When omitted, the number
5: is parsed using CARTESIA_DEFAULT_PHONE_REGION (default: US).
6: """
7: 
8: from __future__ import annotations
9: 
10: import re
11: from typing import Optional
12: 
13: import phonenumbers
14: from phonenumbers import NumberParseException, PhoneNumberFormat
15: 
16: _NON_DIGIT_RE = re.compile(r"[^\d+]+")
17: _FALLBACK_REGION = "US"
18: # Regions tried when no + country code is provided (default region first).
19: _CRM_FALLBACK_REGIONS = ("US", "CA", "IN", "GB", "AU", "MX", "DE", "FR")
20: 
21: 
22: def _format_parsed_number(parsed: phonenumbers.PhoneNumber, *, require_valid: bool) -> Optional[str]:
23:     if require_valid:
24:         if not phonenumbers.is_valid_number(parsed):
25:             return None
26:     elif not phonenumbers.is_possible_number(parsed):
27:         return None
28:     return phonenumbers.format_number(parsed, PhoneNumberFormat.E164)
29: 
30: 
31: def _try_parse_candidate(
32:     candidate: str,
33:     region: Optional[str],
34:     *,
35:     require_valid: bool,
36: ) -> Optional[str]:
37:     try:
38:         parsed = phonenumbers.parse(candidate, region)
39:     except NumberParseException:
40:         return None
41:     return _format_parsed_number(parsed, require_valid=require_valid)
42: 
43: 
44: def try_normalize_phone_to_e164(
45:     raw: str,
46:     *,
47:     default_region: Optional[str] = None,
48: ) -> Optional[str]:
49:     """
50:     Best-effort E.164 normalization for CRM storage.
51: 
52:     Accepts international numbers with or without a + prefix. Tries the configured
53:     default region first, then common regions, preferring valid parses over
54:     possible-only parses. Falls back to a +digits form for 8–15 digit inputs.
55:     """
56:     value = (raw or "").strip()
57:     if not value:
58:         return None
59: 
60:     if value.startswith("00"):
61:         value = "+" + value[2:]
62: 
63:     cleaned = _NON_DIGIT_RE.sub("", value.replace(" ", ""))
64:     if not cleaned:
65:         return None
66: 
67:     if cleaned.startswith("+"):
68:         explicit = "+" + cleaned[1:].lstrip("+")
69:         for require_valid in (True, False):
70:             formatted = _try_parse_candidate(explicit, None, require_valid=require_valid)
71:             if formatted:
72:                 return formatted
73: 
74:     digits = cleaned.lstrip("+")
75:     regions: list[str] = []
76:     default = (default_region or _FALLBACK_REGION).strip().upper()
77:     if not default:
78:         regions.append(default)
79:     for region in _CRM_FALLBACK_REGIONS:
80:         if region not in regions:
81:             regions.append(region)
82: 
83:     valid_matches: list[str] = []
84:     possible_matches: list[str] = []
85:     for region in regions:
86:         formatted = _try_parse_candidate(digits, region, require_valid=True)
87:         if formatted:
88:             valid_matches.append(formatted)
89:             continue
90:         formatted = _try_parse_candidate(digits, region, require_valid=False)
91:         if formatted:
92:             possible_matches.append(formatted)
93: 
94:     if valid_matches:
95:         return valid_matches[0]
96:     if possible_matches:
97:         return possible_matches[-1]
98: 
99:     if len(digits) == 10:
100:         return f"+1{digits}"
101:     if len(digits) == 11 and digits.startswith("1"):
102:         return f"+{digits}"
103:     if 8 <= len(digits) <= 15:
104:         return f"+{digits}"
105:     return None
106: 
107: 
108: def normalize_phone_to_e164(
109:     raw: str,
110:     *,
111:     default_region: Optional[str] = None,
112: ) -> str:
113:     """
114:     Normalize a CRM mobile string to E.164 (e.g. +14155550142).
115: 
116:     Raises:
117:         ValueError: when the number cannot be parsed or is invalid.
118:     """
119:     value = (raw or "").strip()
120:     if not value:
121:         raise ValueError("Mobile number is required.")
122: 
123:     # Allow 00 international prefix (common outside US).
124:     if value.startswith("00"):
125:         value = "+" + value[1:]
126: 
127:     cleaned = _NON_DIGIT_RE.sub("", value.replace(" ", ""))
128:     if cleaned.startswith("+"):
129:         candidate = "+" + cleaned[1:].lstrip("+")
130:         region = None
131:     else:
132:         candidate = cleaned
133:         region = (default_region or _FALLBACK_REGION).strip().upper()
134: 
135:     try:
136:         parsed = phonenumbers.parse(candidate, region)
137:     except NumberParseException as exc:
138:         raise ValueError(
139:             f"Invalid mobile number: {exc}. "
140:             f"Include a country code (e.g. +91…) or set CARTESIA_DEFAULT_PHONE_REGION."
141:         ) from exc
142: 
143:     if not phonenumbers.is_possible_number(parsed):
144:         raise ValueError(
145:             "Mobile number is not a possible phone number. "
146:             "Check the number or set CARTESIA_DEFAULT_PHONE_REGION for your country."
147:         )
148:     if not phonenumbers.is_valid_number(parsed):
149:         raise ValueError(
150:             "Mobile number is not a valid phone number. "
151:             "Check the number or set CARTESIA_DEFAULT_PHONE_REGION for your country."
152:         )
153: 
154:     return phonenumbers.format_number(parsed, PhoneNumberFormat.E164)

(End of file - total 154 lines)

steps.message:
All four field reports traced to two files; four one-line fixes, no test files touched.

## Fixes

**`agent/integrations/cartesia/phone.py`** (used by contact create/update, CSV import, and call initiation)

1. **Configured region ignored for ambiguous numbers** — `try_normalize_phone_to_e164` at phone.py:77 had an inverted condition: `if not default: regions.append(default)`. The workspace's default region was only added to the candidate list when it was *empty*, so US (first entry of the hardcoded fallback tuple) always won ambiguous parses. Now `if default:` puts the configured region first, so a UK workspace parses `020 7946 0958` as `+442079460958` instead of a `+1` number.

2. **`00` access code rejected** — the strict `normalize_phone_to_e164` at phone.py:125 stripped only one character (`value[1:]`), turning `0044...` into `+044...`, which always fails validation with "invalid number". Now `value[2:]`, matching the (already-correct) lenient variant: `0044 7911 123456` → `+447911123456`.

**`agent/services/smbcontacts/loan_types.py`**

3. **Unknown loan-type code mislabeled** — `loan_type_label` fallback at loan_types.py:94 did `replace("_", "").title()`, printing `hard_money` as `"Hardmoney"`. Now `replace("_", " ").title()` → `"Hard Money"`, consistent with the formatters in `lender_match.py` and the PDF report.

4. **Odd-cased known type stored verbatim** — `resolve_loan_type` at loan_types.py:106 matched on `value.lower()` but returned the original `value`, so `"Working_Capital"` was stored as-is instead of the canonical id. Now returns `value.lower()` → `working_capital`.

## Verification

- Direct calls confirm all four reported scenarios now produce correct values, and routine inputs (plain US mobile under US default, dropdown loan-type ids, `+`-prefixed internationals, the Indian-number fallback case) are unchanged.
- `python -m pytest tests -v`: **166 passed, 24 skipped, 7 failed** — the same 7 failures (`test_document_ingestion_readiness`, `test_document_report`, `test_inbound_calls`, `test_ingestion_stale_recovery`) occur on the untouched checkout (verified via `git stash`), so they are pre-existing and unrelated to phone/loan-type logic. All tests covering the modified code paths pass.
